Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned. High-level takeaways from our discovery: Cortex is focused on predictable per-unit inference cost, 95th percentile latency targets for interactive workflows (<400ms), and an easy path to production with observability and fallbacks.

Why Redwood looks compelling for Cortex (short bullets):
- Unit economics: our runtime (batching + KV/prefix caching + quantized model variants) typically reduces effective per-1M token costs by 2–4x vs unmanaged hyperscaler endpoints given comparable latency SLOs. Example illustrative numbers below (we'll validate with your prompts): Redwood hosted baseline: ~$95 / 1M tokens; with caching/batching applied (40–70% effective hit rate) -> effective $30–$45 / 1M tokens. Hyperscaler A (managed inference): ~$200–$260 / 1M tokens for the same model, higher for low-latency configs. Self-hosted raw model CPU/GPU cost might look lower per-token but total TCO is higher once ops, SRE, and utilization inefficiencies are included.
- Production-first controls: reserved (Dedicated) pools, autoscale/burst options, and rollouts to reduce risk during launches.
- Observability & regressions: token-level costs, per-route latency/trace, and evals tied to prompt sets so you can catch quality regressions during model swaps.
- Graceful degradation: automated fallback routing to cheaper variants or other regions when capacity is constrained (keeps products online).

Proposed next tests (we recommend two short runs):
1) Latency-run (low concurrency): 1k requests, measure p50/p90/p95 end-to-end for your representative prompts (we'll target p95 < 400ms).
2) Cost-run (steady throughput): 100k tokens across your prompt mix to observe batching behavior, KV hit rate, and effective $/1M tokens.

What we need from you:
- Share 3–6 representative prompts (including a long-context example if you have one).
- Confirm target latency SLO (you said ~400ms p95; confirm).
- Procurement contact (for a quick quote and standard MSA).

What we'll deliver:
- Detailed TCO model (attached template) with assumptions called out.
- Benchmark results and raw logs (S3) + summary deck.
- Suggested rollout config (batch sizes, cache TTLs, quantization profile).

I attached a starter TCO_model.xlsx and a short benchmark-instructions.md with variables we'll use. Rishi — can you run the latency and cost runs once Alex shares the prompts? Vivek — looping you for approvals/discount guidance if we need a dedicated trial seat.

Next step: Alex, if you can share prompts and procurement contact by Tue EOD (PST), we can run tests Wed–Thu and deliver a results deck by Friday.
